title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 149 (Company to have board of directors)

content.overview: Section 149 fixes the minimum and maximum number of directors, requires resident and, for prescribed companies, independent and woman directors.
content.glance: Section 149 fixes the minimum and maximum number of directors, requires resident and, for prescribed companies, independent and woman directors.
content.study: A public company needs at least three directors, a private company two, and an OPC one, with a maximum of fifteen unless the members authorise more by special resolution. At least one director must have stayed in India for a total of not less than 182 days in the financial year. Listed companies and other prescribed public companies must have independent directors of the prescribed proportion, and at least one woman director. Independent-director criteria and the code in Schedule IV attach to the appointment. An independent director is not entitled to stock options and may be paid sitting fees, reimbursement and profit-related commission as permitted. Liability of an independent director or non-executive director is limited to acts or omissions with their knowledge, consent, connivance, or where they failed to act diligently.
